title: Deep Bacon, Cheese & Spinach Quiche
description: A deep, generous quiche that uses a full 8 eggs. Store-bought pastry keeps it easy, and it packs well for work lunches with a roast veg couscous salad.

items.name: sheets frozen shortcrust pastry
items.prep: thawed 5-10 min on the bench, laid out separately

items.name: large eggs
items.prep: float test first if near their date

items.name: pure or thickened cream
items.prep: or half cream, half milk for a lighter set

method.title: Prep the tin
method.instruction: Unclip a 22-24 cm springform tin, lay baking paper over the base and clip the ring back on so the paper is clamped in. Grease the sides well.

method.title: Line with pastry
method.instruction: Lay one pastry sheet on the base. Cut the second sheet into strips and press them around the wall, overlapping the base by 1 cm and each other at the joins. Press all seams firmly, dabbing with water if needed. Bring the walls up 5-6 cm (higher than you think).

method.title: Prick and chill
method.instruction: Stab the base all over with a fork, every couple of centimetres, right through to the paper. Don't prick the sides. Chill while the oven heats to 200°C (180°C fan).

method.title: Cook the filling
method.instruction: Fry the bacon over medium heat for 5 min, add the onion and cook until soft, about 5 min more. Stir in the spinach until wilted, then let it cool.

method.title: Blind bake
method.instruction: Line the pastry with scrunched baking paper and fill with uncooked rice or lentils, pushed up against the sides. Sit the tin on a baking tray and bake.

method.title: Dry the base
method.instruction: Lift out the paper and weights. Bake until the base looks dry and lightly golden. If a big bubble puffs up, prick it once and press it flat with the back of a fork. Patch any holes with raw pastry scraps. Whisk the eggs, cream, salt, pepper and nutmeg while it bakes.

method.title: Fill and bake
method.instruction: Lower the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Spread the bacon mixture over the base, scatter over the cheese, then pour in the custard, stopping 1 cm below the pastry rim. Bake on the tray until puffed and golden.

method.title: Check doneness
method.instruction: From 40 min, jiggle the tin: the centre should wobble in one piece, like jelly. A knife 3 cm from the centre should come out without runny egg. If not, return for 5 min at a time, laying foil over the top if it's browning too fast.

method.title: Rest and unmould
method.instruction: Rest 15 min, run a knife around the inside of the ring, then unclip it. Cool completely (about 1 hr) before slicing, or chill another hour for the cleanest cuts.

extras.title: Roast veg, chickpea & couscous salad (lunch side, 4 serves)

details.Veg: 1 medium sweet potato (2 cm chunks), 1 zucchini, 1 red capsicum (2-3 cm chunks), 1 red onion (wedges), 1 tin chickpeas (drained and rinsed).
details.Roast: Toss with 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp smoked paprika and 1/2 tsp salt. Roast at 220°C for 30-35 min, turning halfway, before the quiche goes in.
details.Couscous: Pour 250 ml boiling stock over 1 cup couscous, cover 5 min, then fluff immediately with a fork and a drizzle of oil. Spread on a tray so it doesn't clump.
details.Dressing: Juice of 1 lime (or lemon), 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 crushed garlic clove. Toss everything together with parsley if using.
details.Swaps: A 500 g bag of frozen Mediterranean or roast veg mix works too. Roast from frozen, don't thaw.

details.1: 220°C: roast the salad veg. Line the tin, cook the filling and make the couscous meanwhile.
details.2: 200°C: blind bake the pastry once the veg is out.
details.3: 180°C: bake the quiche. Assemble and portion the salad while it bakes.

notes: 8 eggs + 375 ml cream fills a deep springform almost exactly. Make the pastry walls 5-6 cm high, or pour the extra custard into a greased ramekin and bake it alongside for 20-25 min.
Always bake on a tray. Springform seams leak a little, and the tray catches drips.
A deep quiche in a springform took about 55-60 min, longer than the usual 40-45 min.
An infrared thermometer only reads the surface. Use the jiggle and knife tests, or a probe thermometer (75-80°C in the centre).
Thickened cream works as well as pure cream. Heavy or double cream is very rich, so cut it half and half with milk.
Swap the filling for ham, mushroom, capsicum, zucchini, feta or leftover roast veg, keeping it to about 2 cups. Cook watery veg first.
Pack the quiche and salad in separate containers, or the dressing makes the pastry soggy. Both keep 3-4 days in the fridge; the quiche also freezes well in slices.
